newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LE ROUX PASSED FIT TO TOUR WITH SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LE ROUX PASSED FIT TO TOUR WITH SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: Transvaal flyhalf Hennie le Roux has been passed fit to tour Argentina, France and Wales with the Springbok squad in November and December, the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) said on Tuesday.
Le Roux badly bruised his leg during Saturday's Currie Cup final between Transvaal and Natal at Ellis Park and was thought likely to miss the tour after spending the rest of the weekend on crutches.
Subsequent X-rays confirmed there had been no fracture and le Roux's recovery since has been rapid.
"Yes, he's going on tour, he's keen to tour and he will play as soon as he's fit enough," said Paul Dobson, SARFU's media liaison officer for the Argentina tour.

"The injury was not as serious as we initially thought and it would appear that Hennie, after two to three weeks, should start training again and will possibly be fit enough to play after that," SARFU medical consultant Doctor Ismail Jakoet said.
Le Roux has set himself the target of being fit enough to play in the first test against Argentina in Buenos Aires on November 9.
"So far, my period of recovery has been remarkable and I'm hoping to be fit to play in a week to 10 days," le Roux said.

Springbok coach Andre Markgraaff has already lost centre Christiaan Scholtz, loosehead prop Os du Randt, wing Pieter Hendriks and utility back Boeta Wessels from his original 36-man squad because of injury.
